purpose: Question-only adult ambiguity and answerability screen. These are fictional test cases, not customer facts.
reviewBoundary: Judge whether each immediate question contains one understandable, answerable ask and whether every permitted answer, including unknown, has a visible route effect. Do not judge hidden oracle material or infer product efficacy.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether to run a limited AI scheduling pilot or commit the whole care network before the safety and service gates are known.
questions.question: Which failure would make you stop the pilot even if it saves staff time?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Name the incident, complaint or service standard that should define the stopping rule.

routeEffects.routeChange: Bind the limited pilot to the human-defined failure that stops it.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not widen the pilot until a concrete stopping failure is defined.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether the service gain survives the two unsafe schedules and the continuity standard families value.
questions.question: Out of 1,000 scheduled journeys, how many unsafe ones would stop the rollout?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Review the safety baseline and total journey volume before setting the limit.

routeEffects.routeChange: Use the stated unsafe-journey threshold as the human rollout stop rule.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Hold rollout until the baseline and tolerated safety limit are known.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether the pilot can restore complex-care continuity without Elena becoming the permanent exception handler.
questions.question: Out of every 100 vulnerable clients, how many must keep the same carer without you stepping in before expansion?

answerContract.unit: vulnerable clients keeping the same carer
answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Measure continuity for vulnerable clients and record whether Elena had to step in.

routeEffects.routeChange: Expand only after continuity reaches the threshold without Elena rescuing exceptions.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Keep expansion paused until continuity and executive intervention are measured together.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether to move half the firm from bespoke projects into a monthly product before knowing what clients actually renew for.
questions.question: When clients hired you again, what did they mention most: speed, access between projects, or live challenge?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Ask repeat clients which part of the work made them hire Lumen again.

routeEffects.routeChange: Test a faster-answer offer before moving delivery capacity.
Test an access-between-projects offer before moving delivery capacity.
Test a live-challenge offer before moving delivery capacity.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not choose the product promise until repeat-client evidence distinguishes it.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether a repeatable decision-room product can preserve the senior challenge clients renew for without rebuilding a dashboard nobody needs.
questions.question: Have any clients used the monthly product without a senior researcher and said its challenge changed their decision?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Run one paid client decision through the product without a senior researcher, then ask what changed.

routeEffects.routeChange: Continue the repeatable-product route to an economics test using delivered challenge evidence.
Treat the current offer as a senior service until challenge transfers without the researcher.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not call the product scalable until one paid delivered-use test resolves transfer.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether to scale the paid decision-room format after the dashboard route failed, and what proof should unlock moving half the team.
questions.question: How many clients must pay for the new service again before you move half the team?

answerContract.unit: clients who pay for the new service again
answerContract.comparator: the minimum required before moving half the team
answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Model the revenue and delivery capacity at different repeat-purchase counts.

routeEffects.routeChange: Move half the team only after repeat purchase reaches the leader-set threshold.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Keep the capacity move paused until its renewal and economics threshold is set.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether to redesign planning roles and buy the system now, or first test whether data and measures are creating the apparent resistance.
questions.question: If the same planners hit the target with accurate information and fair targets, would you still change their roles?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Use one same-team test before deciding whether the roles must change.

routeEffects.routeChange: Keep role redesign in scope, but require a reason beyond the current performance failure.
Repair information and measures before deciding whether roles must change.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Delay the role conclusion until the same-team test separates people from system conditions.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether one plant can prove the new operating conditions with the same planners before Forgepoint commits all six plants.
questions.question: Will one plant have to hit the delivery target with the same planners before you fund all six?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Name one plant, one delivery target, one time window and the funding decision it controls.

routeEffects.routeChange: Make same-planner target delivery at one plant the gate for funding all six.
Require Jonah to name a different proof gate before group funding can proceed.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not fund all six plants until an owner, target, time window and proof gate are named.

questions.decisionFocus: Which planning work should move to AI after one plant showed the same people can improve when data and measures change.
questions.question: Which named person makes the final call when an AI plan could make a customer late?

options: A named human chosen by the escalation rule
answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Review late-order cases and identify where customer accountability cannot be delegated.

routeEffects.routeChange: Assign the customer-impact exception and final call to a named planner.
Escalate the customer-impact exception and final call to a named operations leader.

routeEffects.answer: A named human chosen by the escalation rule
routeEffects.routeChange: Automate routine planning only inside a rule that names the human exception owner.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not let the plan affect a customer until a human final-call owner is named.

questions.decisionFocus: Whether to fund a precision fan-intelligence system before the campaign has a named audience movement and human creative boundary.
questions.question: Which group of fans must buy more tickets for you to move the GBP 18 million?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Use ticket-buyer and audience evidence to define the group before choosing a route.

routeEffects.routeChange: Judge the GBP 18 million route by ticket growth among franchise-new viewers.
Judge the GBP 18 million route by ticket growth among casual viewers.
Judge the GBP 18 million route by ticket growth among core fans.
Replace the audience gate with the leader-named ticket-buyer group.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Do not choose the campaign route until its intended ticket-buyer group is defined.

questions.decisionFocus: Which exposure route, if either, should receive GBP 18 million after increasing purchases from franchise-new viewers without reducing core-fan purchases.
questions.question: Which route gets the GBP 18 million: character-first, theory-first, or neither until new buyers increase without losing core fans?

answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Compare both routes on new-viewer purchases and core-fan purchases before allocating the budget.

routeEffects.routeChange: Choose character-first only with new-viewer purchase growth and no core-fan purchase loss.
Choose theory-first only with new-viewer purchase growth and no core-fan purchase loss.
Hold the GBP 18 million allocation until the two purchase conditions are tested.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Hold the allocation and run a comparable purchase test across both audience groups.

questions.decisionFocus: What held-out proof should unlock the next major shift after three releases showed audience and sequence matter more than content volume.
questions.question: How many extra new viewers out of 100 must buy a ticket, without core-fan sales falling, before you move GBP 18 million?

answerContract.unit: additional new viewers who buy a ticket
answerContract.evidenceRequestIfUnknown: Measure actual ticket purchases in a held-out test and core-fan sales before setting the gate.

routeEffects.routeChange: Move the GBP 18 million only after new-viewer purchases clear the threshold and core-fan sales do not fall.

unknownRouteEffect.routeChange: Keep the allocation unchanged until purchase lift and the core-fan constraint are measured.
